name: DISABLE ACTIVITY HISTORY (POLICY)
desc: Group-policy switch that stops Windows from recording which apps, files and websites you open (Activity History) and from uploading that history to your Microsoft account.

info.why: Keeps a local and cloud timeline of your activity from being built.
info.gain: Less personal data stored and synced; removes a small amount of background logging.
info.cost: 'Pick up where you left off' suggestions and cross-device activity resume stop working.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't use cross-device activity resume.

name: DISABLE LOCATION FOR ALL USERS
desc: Turns off the device-wide location switch (the top switch in Settings > Privacy > Location), so no account or app on this PC can read your position. The existing Location tweak only affects your own account's apps.

info.why: Stops every user and app from obtaining your physical location.
info.gain: No location lookups (Wi-Fi/IP based or GPS) by any app.
info.cost: Maps, weather, 'Find my device', automatic time zone and any app that needs your location stop getting it.
info.who: Desktop PCs; anyone who never uses location features.

name: DISABLE OFFLINE MAPS AUTO-UPDATE
desc: Stops Windows from automatically downloading updates for offline maps (Settings > Apps > Offline maps).

info.why: Avoids background map downloads you may never use.
info.gain: No automatic map downloads over your connection.
info.cost: Offline maps you downloaded go out of date until you update them by hand.
info.who: Everyone not using the Maps app offline.

name: BLOCK FEEDBACK NOTIFICATIONS (POLICY)
desc: Policy that stops Windows and the Feedback Hub from showing 'How likely are you to recommend Windows…' survey pop-ups for every user.

info.why: Removes unsolicited survey pop-ups.
info.gain: No survey interruptions.
info.cost: None; you can still open Feedback Hub yourself.

name: FEEDBACK FREQUENCY: NEVER
desc: Sets your account's 'Feedback frequency' (Settings > Privacy > Diagnostics & feedback) to Never by setting the survey count to 0 and removing the survey period.

info.why: The per-account counterpart of the feedback policy above.
info.gain: No feedback requests for your account.
info.cost: None.

name: DISABLE WINDOWS ERROR REPORTING
desc: Stops Windows from collecting crash and hang reports for apps and sending them to Microsoft.

info.why: Keeps crash data (which can contain parts of documents in memory) on your PC.
info.gain: No report uploads or WerFault.exe report processing after crashes.
info.cost: Microsoft's 'solutions to problems' stop appearing and developers get no crash reports from you. Blue-screen dump files are still written locally.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't rely on Windows' problem reports.

name: DISABLE ADVERTISING ID (ALL USERS)
desc: Policy that turns off the advertising ID apps use to show personalised ads, for every account on this PC.

info.why: Stops apps from tracking you across apps with a shared ad identifier.
info.gain: Ads in apps become non-personalised.
info.cost: None beyond less relevant ads.

name: DISABLE TAILORED EXPERIENCES
desc: Policy that stops Microsoft from using your diagnostic data to personalise tips, ads and recommendations in Windows.

info.why: Prevents diagnostic data from being used for marketing.
info.gain: Fewer personalised promotions.
info.cost: Tips and suggestions become generic.

name: DISABLE INKING & TYPING PERSONALISATION
desc: Stops Windows from collecting your handwriting and typing patterns (and harvesting your contacts' names) to build a personal dictionary.

info.why: Keeps what you type and write out of Windows' personalisation data.
info.gain: Less typing data collected.
info.cost: Handwriting recognition and text suggestions learn less from you, so they may be less accurate.
info.who: Anyone not using pen handwriting or touch keyboard suggestions.

name: DISABLE TYPING INSIGHTS
desc: Turns off 'Typing insights' (Settings > Time & language > Typing), which records statistics about your typing and autocorrect use.

info.why: Stops typing statistics being collected.
info.gain: Less input data collected.
info.cost: The Typing insights page shows no data.

name: LIMIT DIAGNOSTIC LOG COLLECTION (POLICY)
desc: Policy that stops Windows from collecting additional diagnostic logs when your diagnostic level is Optional.

info.why: Reduces the extra log files sent with optional diagnostic data.
info.gain: Less data uploaded.
info.cost: Microsoft gets less information to diagnose problems on your PC.

name: LIMIT CRASH-DUMP COLLECTION (POLICY)
desc: Policy that limits crash dumps sent with optional diagnostic data to small 'mini' dumps.

info.why: Large memory dumps can contain document contents; this keeps them from being sent.
info.gain: Less sensitive data uploaded.
info.cost: Microsoft gets less detail about crashes.

name: DISABLE DIAGTRACK BOOT LOGGER
desc: Stops the 'Diagtrack-Listener' trace session that starts at boot to buffer telemetry events for the Connected User Experiences (DiagTrack) service from starting at boot (sets its Autologger 'Start' value to 0). The logger's registry key is left in place, so turning this off puts it back exactly.

info.why: Event-trace sessions run constantly from boot and write to disk; this one only serves diagnostics/telemetry.
info.gain: One less trace session and its small, constant disk writes.
info.cost: None for normal use; telemetry events from early boot are not collected.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't need Microsoft diagnostics.

name: DISABLE SQM LOGGER
desc: Stops the 'SQMLogger' session that records Software Quality Metrics (legacy Customer Experience Improvement Program data) from starting at boot (sets its Autologger 'Start' value to 0). The logger's registry key is left in place, so turning this off puts it back exactly.

info.why: Event-trace sessions run constantly from boot and write to disk; this one only serves diagnostics/telemetry.
info.gain: One less trace session and its small, constant disk writes.
info.cost: None for normal use.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't need Microsoft diagnostics.

name: DISABLE SETUP TELEMETRY LOGGER
desc: Stops the 'SetupPlatformTel' session that records telemetry about Windows setup and feature upgrades from starting at boot (sets its Autologger 'Start' value to 0). The logger's registry key is left in place, so turning this off puts it back exactly.

info.why: Event-trace sessions run constantly from boot and write to disk; this one only serves diagnostics/telemetry.
info.gain: One less trace session and its small, constant disk writes.
info.cost: Upgrade problems are harder for Microsoft to diagnose.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't need Microsoft diagnostics.

name: DISABLE OOBE EXPERIENCE LOGGER
desc: Stops the 'CloudExperienceHostOobe' session that logs the out-of-box and first-sign-in screens from starting at boot (sets its Autologger 'Start' value to 0). The logger's registry key is left in place, so turning this off puts it back exactly.

info.why: Event-trace sessions run constantly from boot and write to disk; this one only serves diagnostics/telemetry.
info.gain: One less trace session and its small, constant disk writes.
info.cost: None for normal use.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't need Microsoft diagnostics.

name: DISABLE WI-FI SESSION TRACE
desc: Stops the always-on 'WiFiSession' trace that records Wi-Fi connection events from starting at boot (sets its Autologger 'Start' value to 0). The logger's registry key is left in place, so turning this off puts it back exactly.

info.why: Event-trace sessions run constantly from boot and write to disk; this one only serves diagnostics/telemetry.
info.gain: One less trace session and its small, constant disk writes.
info.cost: The Wi-Fi report (netsh wlan show wlanreport) and network troubleshooter have less history.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't need Microsoft diagnostics.

name: DISABLE NETWORK LIGHTWEIGHT TRACE
desc: Stops the always-on 'LwtNetLog' network diagnostics trace from starting at boot (sets its Autologger 'Start' value to 0). The logger's registry key is left in place, so turning this off puts it back exactly.

info.why: Event-trace sessions run constantly from boot and write to disk; this one only serves diagnostics/telemetry.
info.gain: One less trace session and its small, constant disk writes.
info.cost: The network troubleshooter has less data to work with.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't need Microsoft diagnostics.

name: DISABLE INTERNET CONNECTIVITY PROBES
desc: Stops Windows from contacting www.msftconnecttest.com each time the network changes to check whether it has internet access (policy plus service setting).

info.why: Removes a phone-home request made every time you connect.
info.gain: No connectivity-check traffic to Microsoft.
info.cost: The network icon may show 'No internet' while you are online, captive-portal login pages (hotel/airport Wi-Fi) no longer open automatically, and apps that trust that status (Microsoft Store, Office, Spotify) can think they are offline.
info.who: Privacy-focused desktop users on a home network.

name: DISABLE PEER-TO-PEER UPDATE SHARING
desc: Policy that makes Delivery Optimization download Windows and Store updates from Microsoft only (HTTP mode), never from or to other PCs. Updates themselves keep working.

info.why: Stops your PC from uploading update data to other computers.
info.gain: Your upload bandwidth is never used to serve updates.
info.cost: On a network with several Windows PCs each one downloads updates separately.
info.who: Everyone, especially on metered or slow uploads.

name: DISABLE ENERGY-EFFICIENT ETHERNET
desc: Sets the 'Energy-Efficient Ethernet' (802.3az) advanced property to Disabled on every wired adapter whose driver exposes it.

info.why: The link no longer idles in low-power mode between packets.
info.gain: Can remove small latency spikes and occasional link drops some switch/driver combinations show with EEE.
info.cost: Slightly higher power use (well under a watt per link). Adapters without the setting are left alone.

name: DISABLE ETHERNET FLOW CONTROL
desc: Sets the 'Flow Control' advanced property to Disabled on wired adapters that expose it, so the adapter ignores and never sends Ethernet pause frames.

info.why: Pause frames can briefly stall traffic; some players disable them for steadier latency.
info.gain: No pause-frame stalls.
info.cost: When a switch is congested the adapter may drop packets instead of pausing; TCP resends them, which can lower throughput on busy networks.
info.who: Single-PC home networks; competitive players willing to test.

name: DISABLE INTERRUPT MODERATION
desc: Sets 'Interrupt Moderation' to Disabled on wired adapters, so the adapter signals the CPU for every packet instead of batching them.

info.why: Removes the adapter's batching delay.
info.gain: Packets reach the game a few microseconds sooner; visible in latency benchmarks, usually not noticeable in play.
info.cost: Many more CPU interrupts at high download speeds, which can reduce throughput or cost FPS on slower CPUs.
info.who: Competitive players with fast CPUs who want to test it.
info.note: No guaranteed in-game improvement; measure before and after.

name: DISABLE WAKE-ON-LAN
desc: Disables 'Wake on Magic Packet' and 'Wake on Pattern Match' on wired adapters that expose them.

info.why: Stops network traffic from waking the PC from sleep.
info.gain: No unexpected wake-ups caused by network activity.
info.cost: The PC can't be woken remotely (WoL tools, some NAS or backup schedules).
info.who: Anyone who doesn't wake the PC over the network; laptops.

name: DISABLE NIC VENDOR POWER SAVING
desc: Turns off driver-specific power-saving features on adapters that expose them: Realtek 'Green Ethernet', 'Power Saving Mode', 'Gigabit Lite', 'Advanced EEE', Intel 'Auto Power Saver' and 'Ultra Low Power Mode'. Each adapter only gets the names its own driver uses.

info.why: These features renegotiate link speed or power down parts of the adapter when traffic is low.
info.gain: Avoids brief disconnects or a link that comes back at a lower speed.
info.cost: A little more power use; on laptops on battery that means shorter battery life.

name: LARGER NIC RECEIVE/TRANSMIT BUFFERS
desc: Raises the adapter's 'Receive Buffers' to 2048 and 'Transmit Buffers' to 1024 on wired adapters that expose them.

info.why: Bigger rings give the adapter room to absorb traffic bursts.
info.gain: Fewer dropped packets during bursts such as large downloads while gaming.
info.cost: Uses a few MB more kernel memory. A driver whose maximum is lower normally clamps the value; in rare cases the adapter fails to start until you turn this OFF.
info.who: Wired desktops with heavy network use.

name: DISABLE LARGE SEND OFFLOAD
desc: Disables 'Large Send Offload V2' (IPv4 and IPv6) on wired adapters, so Windows splits outgoing TCP data itself instead of the adapter.

info.why: Some drivers have buggy LSO that causes upload stalls or latency spikes.
info.gain: Can fix slow or bursty uploads on affected drivers.
info.cost: More CPU work when uploading at high speed.

name: DON'T LET WINDOWS TURN OFF THE ADAPTER
desc: Clears 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power' on wired adapters (PnPCapabilities = 24), the same as unticking it in Device Manager.

info.why: Windows can power the adapter down when idle, which some adapters handle badly.
info.gain: Avoids 'network adapter disappeared' or slow-to-reconnect problems after idle or sleep.
info.cost: The adapter stays powered during sleep (slightly higher sleep power on laptops).
info.who: Desktops; anyone who loses Ethernet after sleep.

name: SHORTEN TCP TIME_WAIT TO 30 SECONDS
desc: Closed TCP connections stay reserved for 30 s instead of the default 120 s (TcpTimedWaitDelay).

info.why: Programs that open many short connections can run out of local ports.
info.gain: Ports are freed sooner for download managers, torrent clients and local servers.
info.cost: In theory a very late packet of an old connection could be mixed up with a new one; harmless in normal use.
info.who: Heavy downloaders, developers running local servers.

name: ALLOW DNS-OVER-HTTPS (AUTO-UPGRADE)
desc: Sets the 'Configure DNS over HTTPS name resolution' policy to Allow DoH. When your DNS server is one Windows knows supports DoH (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, Google 8.8.8.8, Quad9 9.9.9.9 and others), lookups go encrypted over HTTPS; otherwise normal DNS is used.

info.why: Encrypts DNS lookups when possible without risking broken name resolution.
info.gain: Your ISP and others on the network can't read or alter lookups sent to supported servers.
info.cost: No effect while you use your ISP's DNS servers. Networks that filter DNS (school, work, parental controls) may stop seeing your lookups.
info.who: Anyone using a public resolver - pairs with 'Use Cloudflare DNS' on the Network page.
info.note: 'Require DoH' is deliberately not offered: with a non-DoH server it breaks all name resolution.

name: DISABLE LLMNR
desc: Policy that turns off Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution, the fallback that broadcasts a name on the local network when DNS can't answer.

info.why: LLMNR is used in well-known attacks to capture password hashes on shared networks.
info.gain: Closes that attack and stops broadcast name lookups.
info.cost: Old devices on the LAN reachable only by LLMNR name stop resolving by name; use their IP or DNS name.
info.who: Everyone, especially laptops on public Wi-Fi.

name: DISABLE SMART MULTI-HOMED NAME RESOLUTION
desc: Policy that stops Windows from sending each DNS query to every network adapter at once and taking the fastest answer.

info.why: With a VPN connected, queries otherwise also go to your normal ISP's DNS (a 'DNS leak').
info.gain: Lookups use one adapter's DNS in order, keeping VPN lookups inside the VPN.
info.cost: If the first adapter's DNS is slow or broken, Windows waits instead of racing another adapter.

name: DISABLE MULTICAST DNS (mDNS)
desc: Turns off Windows' built-in mDNS resolver/responder (names ending in .local).

info.why: mDNS constantly announces and listens on the local network.
info.gain: Less multicast chatter; one less listening service.
info.cost: Devices that announce themselves via mDNS (some printers, Chromecast, smart-home hubs) may stop being found by Windows' own features; apps with their own mDNS (Chrome) are unaffected.

name: DON'T CACHE FAILED DNS LOOKUPS
desc: Windows normally remembers a failed lookup ('name not found') for up to 15 minutes; this sets that time to 0 (MaxNegativeCacheTtl).

info.why: A temporarily failed lookup otherwise keeps failing until the cache entry expires.
info.gain: Sites that were briefly unreachable (after changing DNS or rebooting the router) resolve again immediately.
info.cost: Names that really don't exist are asked again every time (negligible traffic).

name: DISABLE NETBIOS OVER TCP/IP
desc: Sets NetBIOS over TCP/IP to Disabled on every network interface (the 'Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP' option on the WINS tab).

info.why: NetBIOS name broadcasts are an old protocol and an attack surface (NBNS spoofing).
info.gain: No NetBIOS broadcasts; one less legacy protocol listening.
info.cost: Very old devices/NAS boxes reachable only by NetBIOS name, and SMB1-era network browsing, stop resolving. Modern file sharing by DNS name is unaffected. Interfaces added later keep the default.
info.who: Home and laptop users without legacy network devices.

name: BLOCK REMOTE ASSISTANCE INVITATIONS
desc: Unticks 'Allow Remote Assistance connections to this computer' (System Properties > Remote).

info.why: Remote Assistance is a remote-control entry point often abused by tech-support scammers.
info.gain: Nobody can take control through a Remote Assistance invitation.
info.cost: You can't receive Remote Assistance (msra.exe) help. Quick Assist and Remote Desktop are separate.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't use Remote Assistance.

name: DISABLE AUTORUN ON ALL DRIVES
desc: Policy that stops Windows from automatically running anything (autorun.inf) from USB sticks, discs or network drives.

info.why: Autorun is a classic way malware spreads through USB drives.
info.gain: Inserted media can't start programs by itself.
info.cost: Installer discs and some USB gadgets no longer start automatically; open them from File Explorer.

name: DISABLE WINDOWS SCRIPT HOST
desc: Stops .vbs, .vbe, .js and .wsf script files from running through wscript.exe/cscript.exe.

info.why: Script files in emails and downloads are a common malware delivery method.
info.gain: Those scripts can't run.
info.cost: Old installers, login scripts or tools that use VBScript/JScript fail with 'Windows Script Host access is disabled'.
info.who: Home users who don't run VBScript tools.

name: ENABLE LSA PROTECTION
desc: Runs the Local Security Authority (lsass.exe) as a protected process. Value 2 enables it without a UEFI lock, so it can be turned off again.

info.why: Credential-dumping tools read passwords and hashes from lsass memory.
info.gain: Stops non-protected processes from reading lsass memory.
info.cost: Third-party LSA plug-ins (some smart-card, VPN or password-sync tools) must be Microsoft-signed or they stop loading; check Event Viewer > CodeIntegrity after enabling.
info.who: Everyone; already on by default on many new Windows 11 installs.

name: UAC: ALWAYS NOTIFY
desc: Raises User Account Control to the top level: you are also asked when Windows settings are changed, not only when apps request admin rights.

info.why: Malware can silently use auto-elevating Windows tools to bypass the default UAC level.
info.gain: Closes those UAC bypasses.
info.cost: More UAC prompts when changing some Windows settings.
info.note: Turning UAC off entirely (EnableLUA=0) is unsafe and is not offered here.

name: CLEAR PAGE FILE AT SHUTDOWN
desc: Windows overwrites the page file with zeros during shutdown.

info.why: Memory swapped to disk can contain passwords or documents.
info.gain: That data can't be recovered from the drive after shutdown.
info.cost: Shutdown takes longer (seconds to minutes depending on page-file size and drive). Not done for hibernate/Fast Startup.
info.who: Shared or portable PCs without full-disk encryption.

name: REMOVE SMB 1.0 SUPPORT
desc: Disables the 'SMB 1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support' optional feature (client and server parts).

info.why: SMB1 is the protocol exploited by WannaCry and NotPetya.
info.gain: Removes that attack surface.
info.cost: Very old NAS boxes, routers with USB sharing and Windows XP machines that only speak SMB1 can't be reached.
info.who: Everyone (already off by default on clean Windows 11 installs).

name: REMOVE POWERSHELL 2.0 ENGINE
desc: Disables the legacy Windows PowerShell 2.0 engine that still ships beside 5.1 on many installs.

info.why: Attackers start PowerShell 2.0 to bypass script-block logging and antivirus (AMSI) scanning.
info.gain: Closes that downgrade path.
info.cost: Ancient scripts that need -Version 2 stop working. Windows 11 24H2 removed the engine, so it shows as not supported there.

name: WAP PUSH MESSAGE ROUTING
desc: Routes WAP push messages; Windows uses it mainly for device-management (MDM/Intune) enrollment and some diagnostics messaging. This tweak sets the 'dmwappushservice' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: Work/school device enrollment (Intune/MDM) stops working.
info.who: Home PCs not managed by an organisation.

name: DIAGNOSTICS HUB COLLECTOR
desc: Collects real-time ETW traces for Visual Studio's diagnostic tools. This tweak sets the 'diagnosticshub.standardcollector.service' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: Visual Studio's Diagnostic Tools and profiler can't collect data.

name: DOWNLOADED MAPS MANAGER
desc: Manages offline maps for the Maps app. This tweak sets the 'MapsBroker' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: Offline maps can't be downloaded or updated.

name: GEOLOCATION SERVICE
desc: Provides the PC's location to apps. This tweak sets the 'lfsvc' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: No app gets your location; Find my device and automatic time zone stop working.

name: RETAIL DEMO SERVICE
desc: Only used when a PC is put into store-display demo mode. This tweak sets the 'RetailDemo' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: None outside retail demo mode.

name: WINDOWS ERROR REPORTING SERVICE
desc: Processes crash and hang reports. This tweak sets the 'WerSvc' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: Crash reports aren't processed or sent; 'check for solutions' does nothing.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't use problem reports.

name: PROBLEM REPORTS CONTROL PANEL SUPPORT
desc: Backs the Control Panel 'Problem Reports' page. This tweak sets the 'wercplsupport' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.

name: PROGRAM COMPATIBILITY ASSISTANT
desc: Watches programs you run and offers compatibility fixes when an old program fails or installs incorrectly. This tweak sets the 'PcaSvc' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: No automatic compatibility help for legacy software.

name: PRINT SPOOLER
desc: Queues and manages print jobs. This tweak sets the 'Spooler' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: No printing at all - including 'Microsoft Print to PDF' - and printer settings can't be opened.

name: FAX SERVICE
desc: Sends and receives faxes through a fax modem. This tweak sets the 'Fax' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: Windows Fax and Scan can't fax.

name: WINDOWS MEDIA PLAYER NETWORK SHARING
desc: Shares the Windows Media Player library with other devices. This tweak sets the 'WMPNetworkSvc' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.

name: XBOX LIVE GAME SAVE
desc: Syncs saves for Xbox-enabled PC games. This tweak sets the 'XblGameSave' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: Games from the Xbox app/Game Pass can't sync saves to the cloud, so progress may differ between PCs.
info.who: Players who don't use Xbox/Game Pass PC games.

name: GAME DVR & BROADCAST USER SERVICE
desc: Per-user service Game Bar uses to record clips and broadcast. This tweak sets the 'BcastDVRUserService' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: Game Bar recording (Win+Alt+R) and clips stop working.
info.who: Players who record with other software.

name: CAPTURE SERVICE
desc: Lets apps capture the screen through the Windows Graphics Capture API. This tweak sets the 'CaptureService' service to Disabled.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: Snipping Tool (Win+Shift+S), Game Bar capture and screen sharing in some apps stop working.
info.who: Users of third-party capture tools only.

name: CLIPBOARD USER SERVICE

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.

info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.
info.cost: Mobile Hotspot can't be turned on.

info.why: One less service that can start in the background.
info.gain: Slightly less memory and background activity; in most cases a small, not measurable, gain.

desc: Stops Edge sending browsing history to Microsoft to personalise ads, news and other services. (policy PersonalizationReportingEnabled = 0)

info.why: Removes Edge extras you may not want.
info.gain: Less browsing data shared.
info.cost: Less personalised Microsoft news/ads. Edge shows 'Your browser is managed by your organization' while any Edge policy is set; that banner goes away when the last one is turned off.

name: DISABLE FEEDBACK PROMPTS
desc: Removes Edge's 'Send feedback' prompts and smile button. (policy UserFeedbackAllowed = 0)

info.why: Removes Edge extras you may not want.
info.gain: No feedback prompts.
info.cost: You can't send feedback from Edge. Edge shows 'Your browser is managed by your organization' while any Edge policy is set; that banner goes away when the last one is turned off.

name: HIDE NEW TAB NEWS FEED
desc: Hides the Microsoft Start news feed on Edge's New Tab page. (policy NewTabPageContentEnabled = 0)

info.why: Removes Edge extras you may not want.
info.gain: Lighter, faster New Tab page.
info.cost: No news on New Tab. Edge shows 'Your browser is managed by your organization' while any Edge policy is set; that banner goes away when the last one is turned off.

name: SKIP FIRST-RUN SETUP
desc: Hides Edge's first-run setup pages (policy HideFirstRunExperience = 1).

info.why: Skips setup screens.
info.gain: Edge opens straight to a page.
info.cost: You don't get the import/sign-in wizard. Edge shows 'Your browser is managed by your organization' while any Edge policy is set; that banner goes away when the last one is turned off.

name: NO EDGE DESKTOP SHORTCUT AFTER UPDATES
desc: Policy that stops Edge updates from re-creating the Edge shortcut on the desktop.

info.why: Stops a deleted shortcut from coming back.
info.gain: Clean desktop.
info.cost: None.

name: DISABLE BACKGROUND RECORDING
desc: Turns off Game Bar's 'Record what happened' (continuously records the last moments of gameplay).

info.why: Background recording keeps the GPU's video encoder busy during play.
info.gain: Frees GPU encoder time and a little CPU/RAM while gaming.
info.cost: You can't save a clip of something that just happened.
info.who: Players who don't use Game Bar clips.

name: DISABLE GAME BAR CAPTURES (YOUR ACCOUNT)
desc: Turns off the per-user capture switch so Game Bar can't record or screenshot games. The existing 'Disable Game DVR' tweak is the all-users policy.

info.why: Prevents Game Bar capture hooks for your account.
info.gain: No capture overhead from Game Bar.
info.cost: Game Bar recording, screenshots and clips stop working for your account.

name: OPTIMIZATIONS FOR WINDOWED GAMES
desc: Turns on 'Optimizations for windowed games' (Settings > Display > Graphics), which moves older DirectX 10/11 games running windowed or borderless to the modern flip presentation model.

info.why: Older DX10/11 games in borderless mode otherwise use a slower presentation path.
info.gain: Lower input latency in borderless windowed mode, and Auto HDR/VRR support for those games.
info.cost: Rare issues with overlays or capture tools in a few games (you can opt a game out in Graphics settings). This value holds all global graphics options, so it is replaced as a whole and restored as a whole when turned off.
info.who: Players of older DX10/11 games in borderless mode.

name: ALLOW GLOBAL TIMER RESOLUTION REQUESTS
desc: Since Windows 10 2004 a program's request for a finer system timer only affects that program. On Windows 11 this value restores the old behaviour where such a request applies system-wide.

info.why: Timer-resolution utilities rely on it to lower the timer for every program.
info.gain: Some players report steadier frame pacing with a 0.5 ms timer; results vary by game and PC.
info.cost: Higher idle power use and shorter battery life while any program requests a fine timer. No effect unless something requests one.
info.who: Desktop players who use a timer-resolution tool.
info.note: No guaranteed FPS or latency improvement.

name: FAVOUR PERFORMANCE (EPP 0, PLUGGED IN)
desc: Sets 'Processor energy performance preference policy' to 0 % for the active power plan on AC power. Modern Intel and AMD CPUs use this hint to decide how quickly to raise clocks.

info.why: The CPU ramps clocks up faster and holds them under light load.
info.gain: Snappier response; fewer clock ramp-up delays.
info.cost: Higher idle power and temperatures, more fan noise. The battery value is left alone.
info.note: Applies to the plan active when you turn it on; switching to another plan shows this tweak as OFF.

name: HYBRID CPUs: PREFER PERFORMANCE CORES
desc: Sets the documented 'Heterogeneous thread scheduling policy' and its short-running-thread counterpart to 'Prefer performant processors' for the active plan on AC power.

info.why: On CPUs with P-cores and E-cores the scheduler may put foreground work on slower E-cores.
info.gain: Threads go to P-cores first when they are free.
info.cost: More power use; background work also lands on P-cores. No effect on CPUs without E-cores.
info.who: Intel 12th-gen and newer hybrid CPUs, plugged in.

name: DISABLE SYSMAIN (SUPERFETCH)
desc: Stops the service that preloads frequently used apps into RAM and tunes memory and boot prefetching.

info.why: Some users see heavy disk activity from SysMain right after boot.
info.gain: Less background disk and memory activity.
info.cost: Frequently used apps can start slower, especially from a hard disk; boot prefetching stops. Memory compression can no longer be changed while it is off.
info.who: PCs with fast SSDs and plenty of RAM.

name: GROUP SVCHOST SERVICES
desc: Raises the RAM threshold above which Windows runs each service in its own svchost.exe, so services are grouped into fewer processes again (as on low-RAM PCs).

info.why: Dozens of svchost.exe processes each carry some overhead.
info.gain: Fewer processes and slightly lower memory use.
info.cost: If one service crashes it can take the others in its svchost with it, and Task Manager can't show per-service CPU use as precisely.

name: DISABLE MEMORY COMPRESSION
desc: Turns off compression of rarely used memory pages (the 'Memory Compression' process).

info.why: Compressing and decompressing pages costs CPU time.
info.gain: Saves that CPU time.
info.cost: With less than about 16 GB of RAM, Windows pages to disk sooner, which is far slower than compression. Needs the SysMain service running to change.
info.who: PCs with 32 GB or more RAM.

name: DISABLE PAGE COMBINING
desc: Stops Windows from periodically scanning RAM for identical pages to merge them.

info.why: The scan is periodic background work.
info.gain: Removes that background scan.
info.cost: Slightly higher memory use.

name: DISABLE APP PRE-LAUNCH
desc: Stops Windows from starting Store apps (Mail, Photos and others) suspended in the background so they open faster.

info.why: Pre-launched apps sit in memory even if you never open them.
info.gain: Fewer suspended apps in memory.
info.cost: Those apps open a bit slower.
info.who: Users who rarely use Store apps.

name: KEEP KERNEL & DRIVERS IN RAM
desc: Prevents Windows from paging kernel-mode code and drivers out to the page file.

info.why: Paged-out kernel code must be read back from disk when needed.
info.gain: Avoids rare stalls after the PC has been idle.
info.cost: A few hundred MB less RAM for apps; little measurable benefit on PCs with plenty of RAM.
info.who: PCs with 16 GB or more RAM.

name: ENABLE LONG FILE PATHS
desc: Lets programs that support it use paths longer than 260 characters.

info.why: Fixes 'path too long' errors.
info.gain: Deep folder trees, npm/git projects and archives work.
info.cost: Programs without long-path support still fail on such paths; nothing breaks.

name: DISABLE NTFS LAST-ACCESS TIMESTAMPS
desc: Stops NTFS updating each file's 'last accessed' time when it is read (0x80000001 = set by the user, disabled).

info.why: Every file read otherwise causes a small metadata write.
info.gain: Fewer writes when reading many files.
info.cost: Tools that rely on 'last accessed' dates (e.g. Storage Sense's 'not opened for X days') see stale dates. Windows already disables it on large volumes by default.

name: STOP CREATING 8.3 SHORT FILE NAMES
desc: New files no longer get an extra DOS-style short name (like PROGRA~1). Existing short names stay.

info.why: Short names are generated for every new file.
info.gain: Faster file creation in folders with many similar names.
info.cost: Very old 16-bit/DOS-era installers and tools that need short names may fail on new files.

name: MORE NTFS CACHE MEMORY
desc: Raises the paged-pool memory NTFS may use for its metadata cache (NtfsMemoryUsage = 2).

info.why: NTFS metadata is cached in paged pool.
info.gain: Can help with very large numbers of files (big repos, game assets).
info.cost: More kernel memory use; little effect on typical use.
info.who: PCs with lots of RAM and many files.

name: NO THUMBS.DB ON NETWORK FOLDERS
desc: Stops File Explorer writing hidden thumbs.db thumbnail caches into network shares.

info.why: thumbs.db files clutter shares and lock folders.
info.gain: No stray thumbs.db files and no 'file in use' when deleting network folders.
info.cost: Thumbnails for network files are generated again each visit.

name: PCI EXPRESS LINK POWER SAVING OFF (PLUGGED IN)
desc: Sets 'Link State Power Management' to Off for the active plan on AC power, so PCIe links (GPU, NVMe, network) never drop into low-power states.

info.why: Waking a PCIe link from a low-power state adds a small delay.
info.gain: Removes those wake-up delays.
info.cost: A few watts more at idle.

name: USB 3 LINK POWER MANAGEMENT OFF (PLUGGED IN)
desc: Sets 'USB 3 Link Power Management' to Off for the active plan on AC power.

info.why: Some USB 3 devices stutter or disconnect when the link sleeps.
info.gain: Steadier USB audio interfaces, capture cards, external SSDs and wireless dongles.
info.cost: Slightly more power use.

name: DISABLE FILTER KEYS SHORTCUT
desc: Stops holding Right Shift for 8 seconds from turning on Filter Keys (which makes the keyboard ignore quick or repeated presses).

info.why: The shortcut triggers by accident in games.
info.gain: No surprise accessibility pop-up or sluggish keyboard mid-game.
info.cost: The shortcut can't turn Filter Keys on (Settings still can).

name: DISABLE TOGGLE KEYS SHORTCUT
desc: Stops holding Num Lock for 5 seconds from turning on Toggle Keys (beeps on Caps/Num/Scroll Lock).

info.why: The shortcut triggers by accident.
info.gain: No surprise pop-up.
info.cost: The shortcut can't turn Toggle Keys on (Settings still can).

name: SHORTEST KEY-REPEAT DELAY
desc: Sets the keyboard 'Repeat delay' to the shortest step (about 250 ms instead of the default 500 ms).

info.why: Held keys start repeating sooner.
info.gain: Faster key repeat in editors and some games.
info.cost: Accidental repeated characters if you hold keys a bit long.

name: DISABLE WINDOWS INK WORKSPACE
desc: Policy that turns off the pen workspace/pen menu.

info.why: Removes a pen feature on PCs without a pen.
info.gain: No pen menu or its taskbar button.
info.cost: Pen shortcuts from the pen menu stop; pen input itself still works.

name: LOWER MMCSS BACKGROUND RESERVE TO 10 %
desc: The Multimedia Class Scheduler reserves a share of CPU for low-priority work while multimedia threads (audio, games registered with MMCSS) run. The default is 20 %; this sets the documented minimum of 10 %.

info.why: Multimedia threads registered with MMCSS can use more CPU.
info.gain: Up to 90 % instead of 80 % CPU for those threads.
info.cost: Background tasks get less CPU while media plays.
info.note: Evidence of in-game gains is anecdotal.

name: SHOW ONLY AN OUTLINE WHILE DRAGGING WINDOWS
desc: Unticks 'Show window contents while dragging'.

info.why: Dragging large windows redraws them continuously.
info.gain: Smoother dragging on weak GPUs and remote sessions.
info.cost: You see a frame instead of the window while moving it.

name: NO DROP SHADOWS ON DESKTOP ICON LABELS
desc: Removes the drop shadow behind desktop icon labels.

info.why: One less visual effect.
info.gain: Marginally less drawing on the desktop.
info.cost: Labels can be harder to read on busy wallpapers.

name: DETECT 'NOT RESPONDING' APPS SOONER
desc: Windows marks a window as 'Not responding' after 2 seconds without response instead of 5.

info.why: Frozen apps can be closed sooner.
info.gain: Faster 'Not responding' detection.
info.cost: Apps that briefly freeze (loading large files) are labelled 'Not responding' more often.

name: FASTER SHUTDOWN: 2 s SERVICE TIMEOUT
desc: At shutdown Windows waits 2 seconds (default 5) for each service to stop before ending it.

info.why: Shutdowns can hang on a slow service.
info.gain: Shutdown finishes sooner.
info.cost: A service that needs longer to save its state (databases, some VPN/backup agents) can be stopped before it finishes.

name: FASTER HOVER TOOLTIPS & PREVIEWS
desc: Hover delay of 100 ms instead of 400 ms for tooltips, taskbar previews and hover-to-open menus.

info.why: Hover UI appears sooner.
info.gain: Quicker tooltips and taskbar previews.
info.cost: Tooltips and previews pop up more readily while moving the mouse.

name: NO DELAY FOR STARTUP APPS
desc: Windows normally waits about 10 seconds after sign-in before launching startup apps; this starts them immediately.

info.why: Tray apps are ready sooner after sign-in.
info.gain: Chat, sync and mouse software available right away.
info.cost: More programs compete with Explorer right after sign-in, so the desktop can feel busy for a moment.

name: DON'T AUTO-SIGN-IN AFTER UPDATES
desc: Policy that stops Windows using your sign-in info to automatically finish setup and lock the PC after an update restart.

info.why: Your session isn't started automatically after an update.
info.gain: Nothing runs as you until you sign in.
info.cost: After an update restart, apps and settings finish loading only after you sign in.

name: POLICY: NO STORE APPS IN THE BACKGROUND
desc: Policy 'Let Windows apps run in the background' = Force Deny, for every user. On Windows 11 the per-user switch the existing tweak uses no longer covers all apps; this policy does.

info.why: Store apps otherwise run background tasks when closed.
info.gain: Less background CPU, memory and network use.
info.cost: Store apps (Mail, Calendar, Phone Link, some games) can't send live notifications or sync while closed.
info.who: Users who don't rely on Store-app notifications.

name: REMOVE WORK FOLDERS CLIENT
desc: Disables the Work Folders client that syncs files with a company Windows Server. The feature's files stay on disk, so turning this OFF re-enables it without downloading anything.

info.why: Removes an unused Windows component.
info.gain: One less component loaded or indexed.
info.cost: You can't sync with a Work Folders server.

name: REMOVE INTERNET PRINTING CLIENT
desc: Disables printing to printers over HTTP/IPP via a URL. The feature's files stay on disk, so turning this OFF re-enables it without downloading anything.

info.why: Removes an unused Windows component.
info.gain: One less component loaded or indexed.
info.cost: IPP/URL printers can't be added; USB and normal network printers still work.

name: REMOVE XPS SERVICES
desc: Disables the XPS document writer and XPS printing services. The feature's files stay on disk, so turning this OFF re-enables it without downloading anything.

info.why: Removes an unused Windows component.
info.gain: One less component loaded or indexed.
info.cost: The 'Microsoft XPS Document Writer' printer disappears.

name: REMOVE TIFF IFILTER
desc: Disables the filter that lets Windows Search read text inside TIFF images (OCR). The feature's files stay on disk, so turning this OFF re-enables it without downloading anything.

info.why: Removes an unused Windows component.
info.gain: One less component loaded or indexed.
info.cost: Text in scanned TIFF files isn't searchable.

name: DISABLE NVIDIA TELEMETRY
desc: Sets the NVIDIA driver's 'SendTelemetryData' flag to 0, opts out of NVIDIA Control Panel data collection and turns off three NVIDIA feature-telemetry flags (RID44231/64640/66610).

info.why: Reduces usage data sent to NVIDIA.
info.gain: Less data collection; no effect on performance.
info.cost: None known.

name: DISABLE AMD SOFTWARE AUTO-UPDATE CHECKS
desc: Turns off AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition's automatic update check.

info.why: Stops update pop-ups in AMD Software.
info.gain: No background update checks.
info.cost: You must check for driver updates yourself.

name: OPEN FILE EXPLORER TO THIS PC
desc: File Explorer opens to 'This PC' (drives) instead of Home.

info.why: Drives are one click closer.
info.gain: Faster to reach your drives.
info.cost: Home's recent files and favourites are one click further away.

name: ALWAYS SHOW FILE-COPY DETAILS
desc: File copy/move dialogs always open in 'More details' mode with the speed graph.

info.why: See transfer speed and remaining items without clicking.
info.gain: More information during copies.
info.cost: None.

name: NO AUTOMATIC RESTART WHILE SIGNED IN
desc: Policy 'No auto-restart with logged on users': Windows Update installs updates but waits for you to restart instead of restarting on its own while someone is signed in.

info.why: Stops updates from restarting the PC in the middle of a game, download or render.
info.gain: No surprise restarts while you are signed in.
info.cost: Installed updates only take effect once you restart, so you have to restart yourself now and then.
info.who: Everyone who leaves the PC on.

name: ASK BEFORE DOWNLOADING UPDATES
desc: Policy 'Configure Automatic Updates' set to 'Notify for download and auto install': Windows Update tells you when updates are available and only downloads them when you start it from Settings.

info.why: Keeps update downloads from using your connection or disk while you play.
info.gain: Updates download only when you choose.
info.cost: Security fixes wait until you install them: check Windows Update regularly.
info.who: Users on slow or capped connections who update by hand.

name: SKIP THE MALICIOUS SOFTWARE REMOVAL TOOL
desc: Stops Windows Update from offering the monthly Malicious Software Removal Tool (MRT), which runs a background scan after it installs.

info.why: The monthly tool runs a scan in the background after each Patch Tuesday.
info.gain: No monthly MRT download and background scan.
info.cost: One fewer second-opinion malware scan; Microsoft Defender or your antivirus still protects you.
info.who: PCs with an antivirus that is kept up to date.

name: DON'T GET UPDATES AS SOON AS THEY'RE AVAILABLE
desc: Turns off 'Get the latest updates as soon as they're available' (Settings > Windows Update), so new features arrive with the normal monthly updates instead of early.

info.why: Early feature updates are the ones most likely to bring new bugs.
info.gain: New Windows features arrive later, once they have been tested more widely.
info.cost: You get new features a little later than other people.
info.who: Everyone who prefers stability over new features.

name: TELL ME WHEN A RESTART IS NEEDED
desc: Turns on 'Notify me when a restart is required to finish updating' (Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options).

info.why: Pairs with the no-automatic-restart setting so you know when updates are waiting.
info.gain: A notification when an update needs a restart.
info.cost: One more notification after some updates.
info.who: Everyone who restarts the PC themselves.

name: NO NOTIFICATIONS ON THE LOCK SCREEN
desc: Turns off 'Show notifications on the lock screen' and 'Show reminders and incoming VoIP calls on the lock screen' (Settings > System > Notifications).

info.why: Message previews on the lock screen can be read by anyone near the PC.
info.gain: Nothing shows on the lock screen until you sign in.
info.cost: You don't see reminders or calls until you unlock the PC.
info.who: Everyone, especially shared or office PCs.

name: SILENT NOTIFICATIONS
desc: Turns off 'Allow notifications to play sounds' (Settings > System > Notifications). Banners still appear, without the chime.

info.why: Notification chimes cut into game and voice-chat audio.
info.gain: Notifications stay silent.
info.cost: You may miss a notification if you're not looking at the screen.

name: NO BADGES ON TASKBAR APPS
desc: Turns off 'Show badges on taskbar apps' (the unread counters on taskbar icons).

info.why: Unread counters pull your attention to the taskbar.
info.gain: A calmer taskbar.
info.cost: You don't see unread counts for mail and chat apps.

name: NO FLASHING TASKBAR APPS
desc: Turns off 'Show flashing on taskbar apps', so apps that want your attention no longer flash orange in the taskbar.

info.why: Flashing taskbar buttons are distracting, especially across a second monitor while you play.
info.gain: No flashing taskbar buttons.
info.cost: An app waiting for you (a finished download, a chat message) is easier to miss.

name: DON'T LOWER OTHER SOUNDS DURING CALLS
desc: Sets 'When Windows detects communications activity' (Sound Control Panel > Communications) to 'Do nothing', so game and music volume no longer drops by 80% when a voice app opens the microphone.

info.why: Windows treats Discord, Teams and in-game voice as 'calls' and turns everything else down.
info.gain: Game audio stays at full volume while you talk.
info.cost: Other sounds stay loud during real calls; turn them down yourself.

name: NO WINDOWS STARTUP SOUND
desc: Turns off 'Play Windows Startup sound'.

info.why: A quieter start, for example at night.
info.gain: No startup chime.
info.cost: None.

name: SEPARATE BLUETOOTH HEADPHONE VOLUME
desc: Turns off Bluetooth 'absolute volume', so Windows' volume and your headphones' own volume are separate again.

info.why: With absolute volume, some headsets are far too loud at low settings or jump in volume.
info.gain: Finer volume control on headsets that misbehave.
info.cost: You may need to set the volume on both the PC and the headphones.
info.who: Bluetooth headphone users with volume problems.

name: UAC PROMPTS WITHOUT DIMMING THE SCREEN
desc: Shows User Account Control prompts on your normal desktop instead of the dimmed secure desktop (the 'Notify me only when apps try to make changes (do not dim my desktop)' level).

info.why: Switching to the secure desktop flickers the screen and minimises full-screen games.
info.gain: Prompts appear instantly, without the screen going dark.
info.cost: Other programs running as you could interact with the prompt; the secure desktop prevents that.
info.who: Users who want fewer interruptions and accept a little less protection.

name: DON'T LIST ADMINISTRATOR ACCOUNTS IN UAC PROMPTS
desc: Policy 'Enumerate administrator accounts on elevation': off. When a standard user is asked for an administrator password, the prompt no longer lists the administrator accounts; the account name must be typed.

info.why: Listing admin account names helps someone guessing passwords.
info.gain: Admin account names are not shown in prompts.
info.cost: Standard users have to type the admin account name as well as the password.

name: UAC FOR THE BUILT-IN ADMINISTRATOR
desc: Policy 'Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account': on. The hidden built-in 'Administrator' account gets UAC prompts like every other admin account instead of running everything with full rights.

info.why: Anything run by the built-in Administrator otherwise gets full rights silently.
info.gain: The built-in Administrator is protected by UAC too.
info.cost: Only matters if you use the built-in Administrator account; it then sees UAC prompts.
info.who: PCs where the built-in Administrator account is enabled.

name: DON'T SHARE YOUR LANGUAGE LIST WITH WEBSITES
desc: Turns off 'Let websites show me locally relevant content by accessing my language list'.

info.why: Your language list adds to the fingerprint websites can build of you.
info.gain: Websites can't read your Windows language list.
info.cost: Some sites may not pick your language automatically.

name: DISABLE CLIPBOARD SYNC ACROSS DEVICES
desc: Policy 'Allow Clipboard synchronization across devices': off. What you copy is no longer uploaded to sync with your other devices.

info.why: Copied passwords and text are otherwise uploaded to your Microsoft account.
info.gain: Nothing you copy leaves the PC.
info.cost: You can't paste on another device what you copied here.
info.who: Everyone who doesn't paste across devices.

name: DISABLE FIND MY DEVICE
desc: Policy 'Turn On/Off Find My Device': off. The PC no longer reports its location to your Microsoft account for Find my device.

info.why: Find my device periodically sends the PC's location to Microsoft.
info.gain: No location reports to your account.
info.cost: You can't locate or lock the PC from account.microsoft.com if it's lost or stolen.
info.who: Desktop PCs that never leave the house.

name: DISABLE SETTINGS SYNC
desc: Policy 'Do not sync': Windows stops syncing your settings (theme, passwords, language, accessibility) to your Microsoft account.

info.why: Settings are otherwise uploaded and copied to every PC you sign in to.
info.gain: Settings stay on this PC.
info.cost: A new PC you sign in to won't pick up this PC's settings.
info.who: Users with one PC, or who set each PC up themselves.

name: WI-FI ADAPTER AT MAXIMUM PERFORMANCE (PLUGGED IN)
desc: Sets the power plan's 'Wireless Adapter Settings > Power Saving Mode' to Maximum Performance when plugged in.

info.why: Wi-Fi power saving can add latency spikes in online games.
info.gain: Steadier Wi-Fi latency when plugged in.
info.cost: Slightly more power use when plugged in; battery behaviour is unchanged.

name: VIDEO PLAYBACK FAVOURS QUALITY (PLUGGED IN)
desc: Sets the power plan's 'Multimedia settings > Video playback quality bias' to performance when plugged in.

info.why: Windows may lower video quality to save power.
info.gain: Full-quality video playback when plugged in.
info.cost: Slightly more power use during video when plugged in.

name: HIGHER CPU AND GPU PRIORITY FOR GAMES (MMCSS)
desc: Sets the multimedia scheduler's 'Games' task to High scheduling category, priority 6 and GPU priority 8, which games that register with MMCSS get.

info.why: Gives game threads registered with MMCSS an edge over background work.
info.gain: Can reduce stutter while things run in the background.
info.cost: Only affects games that use MMCSS; the effect is small on fast PCs.

name: XBOX BUTTON DOESN'T OPEN GAME BAR
desc: Turns off 'Open Game Bar using this button on a controller', so pressing the Xbox button doesn't pop up Game Bar in the middle of a game.

info.why: The Xbox button is easy to press by accident and pauses the game behind an overlay.
info.gain: No accidental Game Bar pop-ups.
info.cost: You open Game Bar with Win+G instead.

name: HIDE THE COPILOT BUTTON
desc: Turns off 'Copilot' under Settings > Personalisation > Taskbar > Taskbar items.

info.why: Frees taskbar space if you don't use Copilot.
info.gain: One fewer taskbar button.
info.cost: You open Copilot from Start instead.

name: NEVER COMBINE BUTTONS ON OTHER TASKBARS
desc: Sets 'Combine taskbar buttons and hide labels on other taskbars' to Never, for the taskbars on your second and further monitors.

info.why: Shows each window as its own labelled button on extra monitors.
info.gain: Easier switching between windows of the same app.
info.cost: Buttons take more room on those taskbars.

name: MORE PINS IN START
desc: Sets the Start layout to 'More pins' (Settings > Personalisation > Start), so a row more of pinned apps shows and the Recommended section shrinks.

info.why: Fits more of your own apps on the first page of Start.
info.gain: More pinned apps without scrolling.
info.cost: Fewer recommended files are shown.

name: HIDE RECENTLY ADDED APPS IN START
desc: Policy 'Remove Recently added list from Start Menu': newly installed apps are no longer listed at the top of Start.

info.why: Keeps the top of Start for your own apps.
info.gain: A tidier Start menu.
info.cost: New apps aren't highlighted; find them in All apps.

name: SHOW THE FULL PATH IN THE TITLE BAR
desc: Turns on 'Display the full path in the title bar' (Folder Options > View).

info.why: Shows exactly which folder a window is in.
info.gain: Full folder path in the title and on taskbar previews.
info.cost: None.

name: DON'T SHOW RECENT FILES AND FOLDERS IN HOME
desc: Turns off 'Show recently used files' and 'Show frequently used folders' (Folder Options > General > Privacy).

info.why: Anyone looking at your screen sees what you opened recently.
info.gain: Home and Quick access only show what you pinned.
info.cost: No quick way back to recent files from Explorer.

name: NO ADS IN FILE EXPLORER
desc: Turns off 'Show sync provider notifications' (Folder Options > View), the banners that advertise OneDrive and Microsoft 365 inside File Explorer.

info.why: Removes promotional banners from File Explorer.
info.gain: No OneDrive or Microsoft 365 adverts in Explorer.
info.cost: None.

name: NO '- SHORTCUT' ON NEW SHORTCUTS
desc: Stops Windows adding ' - Shortcut' to the name of every shortcut you create.

info.why: Saves renaming every shortcut you make.
info.gain: Shortcuts keep the original name.
info.cost: None.
